evals.prompt: What's the newest safe version of express I can upgrade to?
evals.expected_output: The newest version of express with no known vulns, capped at --max-major-bump 1 by default, with the vulnerable interval skipped called out.
expectations: Runs `vulnetix vdb versions express --ecosystem npm -o json` piped through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_lib/jq/versions.jq`
Runs `vulnetix vdb vulns express -o json` piped through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_lib/jq/vulns.jq` in parallel
Renders the four-line block: Currently installed / Latest published / Recommended safe / Major-bump cap
Calls out the skipped vulnerable interval, e.g. `(skipping vulnerable: 4.16.0–4.17.2 affected by CVE-...)`
Does NOT modify any manifest — this skill is read-only and suggests `/vulnetix:fix` or `/vulnetix:dep-resolve` to apply

evals.prompt: Find me a safe lodash version without any major-version bump from what we have pinned.
evals.expected_output: Newest safe lodash version with --max-major-bump 0 enforced, staying within the current major.
expectations: Applies `--max-major-bump 0` so only patch and minor bumps within the current major are considered
Calls `vulnetix vdb purl "pkg:npm/lodash@latest" -o json` to confirm latest published version
Excludes pre-release tags (-beta, -rc) from the safe set by default
Filters out entries with empty `ecosystem` string returned by `vdb versions` (CVE-affected versions that don't map to a registry)
Reports clearly if no safe version exists under the major-bump cap, rather than recommending a major upgrade
Does not write to `.vulnetix/memory.yaml` — read-only skill

evals.prompt: I need to build a pnpm overrides block pinning urllib3 to a clean version — what should I target?
evals.expected_output: The newest safe pypi version of urllib3 with the vulnerable ranges enumerated, ready to drop into a pnpm/yarn/uv override block.
expectations: Scopes `vdb versions` with `--ecosystem pypi` (since urllib3 exists in multiple ecosystems by name)
For each candidate version, marks it unsafe if any known vuln's affected range includes it
Returns the NEWEST safe version (not the lowest-risk); notes the second-newest is available for risk-averse soak time
Suggests `/vulnetix:fix` or `/vulnetix:dep-resolve` as the follow-up to actually wire the override
Honors `--include-prerelease` only when the user explicitly opts in
Does not perform any manifest writes or memory writes
